metaDescription: Free online .gitlab-ci.yml generator. Create lint, test, build and deploy stages for Node, Python, Go, Maven, Ruby, PHP or Docker, with caching.
intro: Generate a .gitlab-ci.yml with lint, test, build and optional deploy stages for Node, Python, Go, Maven, Ruby, PHP or Docker builds, including dependency caching and merge-request pipelines.
why:
A first GitLab pipeline is mostly boilerplate: choosing an image, installing dependencies, caching them correctly, and wiring stages in order. Getting the cache key and the merge-request rules right is the part people usually look up every time.

Pick your stack and version, choose which stages you need, and the tool writes a pipeline with sensible commands for that stack, a cache keyed on your lock file, and optional workflow rules that avoid duplicate pipelines for branches with open merge requests. Deploy can be GitLab Pages, a manual production job or an automatic one on the default branch. The commands are defaults such as npm test, so adapt them to your project. Nothing is uploaded; it all runs in your browser.
howTo: Choose your stack and enter the image version or tag.
Tick the stages you want: lint, test and build.
Pick a deploy option and the build output folder if you use GitLab Pages.
Copy the YAML into .gitlab-ci.yml and edit the commands to match your project.

faq.q: What commands does each stack use?
faq.a: Sensible defaults, such as npm ci, npm run lint and npm test for Node, or pytest and ruff for Python. Replace them with your own scripts if your project differs.

faq.q: What do the merge-request pipeline rules do?
faq.a: They run pipelines for merge request events and avoid running a second branch pipeline when a merge request is already open, which prevents duplicate jobs.
The cache key is based on your lock file, such as package-lock.json or go.sum, so it refreshes when dependencies change. The cached paths depend on the stack.

faq.q: Is the deploy job ready to use?
faq.a: Pages deploys the build output folder. The production deploy options contain a placeholder echo command, which you must replace with your real deployment steps.
